# scylladbcloud_vector_search (Resource)

Vector search nodes in a cluster datacenter.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Add two vector search nodes to a cluster's datacenter.
resource "scylladbcloud_vector_search" "example" {
	cluster_id = 1337
	datacenter = "AWS_US_EAST_1"
	node_count = 2
	node_type  = "r7g.large"
}

output "scylladbcloud_vector_search_status" {
	value = scylladbcloud_vector_search.example.status
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (Number) Cluster ID.
- `datacenter` (String) Datacenter name, e.g. AWS_US_EAST_1.
- `node_count` (Number) Number of vector search nodes, spread evenly across the cluster's racks (1-27).
- `node_type` (String) Instance type of the vector search nodes, e.g. r7g.large.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `availability_zones` (List of String) Availability zone IDs that hold vector search nodes.
- `datacenter_id` (Number) Datacenter ID.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `status` (String) Health of vector search: HEALTHY, DEGRADED, UNHEALTHY or UNKNOWN.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by <cluster_id>:<datacenter_id>.
terraform import scylladbcloud_vector_search.example 1337:42
```
